learningObjectives: Identify the major components of the Auditory System.
Explain how the Auditory System contributes to sensation, regulation or behaviour.
Connect Auditory System function with clinically relevant symptoms.
Use lesion patterns and phenomenology cautiously rather than relying on one-to-one explanations.

anatomy.label: Cochlea
anatomy.detail: Basilar-membrane mechanics separate frequencies; hair cells encode vibration.
anatomy.clinical: Hair-cell injury causes sensorineural hearing loss.

anatomy.label: Auditory nerve
anatomy.detail: Spiral ganglion axons transmit cochlear output to brainstem.
anatomy.clinical: Neuropathy can disrupt timing despite preserved outer hair-cell function.

anatomy.label: Superior olivary complex
anatomy.detail: Compares interaural timing and level differences.

anatomy.label: Inferior colliculus
anatomy.clinical: Contributes to orienting toward salient sounds.

anatomy.label: Auditory cortex
anatomy.detail: Temporal cortex represents complex acoustic patterns and speech features.
anatomy.clinical: Lesions can impair recognition despite intact peripheral hearing.
